# Sparkform API reference

Everything the addon exposes: the `Sparkform` autoload that spawns and recycles effects, and the base classes an effect script builds on. Property tables for the individual effects live in [EFFECTS.md](EFFECTS.md).

## `Sparkform` autoload

Global spawner and recycler for Sparkform.

Registered as the `Sparkform` autoload. Every effect scene is
instantiated once and then reused from a per-scene pool, so fireworks-heavy
gameplay does not churn the scene tree.


```gdscript
Sparkform.hit_spark(enemy.global_position, Vector2.UP)
Sparkform.explosion(boss.global_position, {"radius": 120.0})
Sparkform.lightning(caster.global_position, target.global_position, {"branches": 4})
Sparkform.cooldown_ring(ability_icon_node, 2.5)
Sparkform.chain(caster.global_position, [a.global_position, b.global_position])
Sparkform.vortex(charge_point, {"radius": 120.0})
```


Effects are parented to a dedicated `Sparkform_Layer` node under the
current scene, so they are never batched into gameplay containers and are
cleaned up automatically on scene changes.

### Signals

| Signal | Description |
|---|---|
| `effect_spawned` | Emitted right after an effect has been placed and started. |
| `effect_finished` | Emitted when an effect finishes, whether it ran to completion or was stopped. |

### Settings

**Pooling**

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pool_size_per_effect` | `int` | `24` | Maximum number of idle instances kept per effect scene. Finished effects beyond this budget are freed instead of pooled. |
| `max_active_effects` | `int` | `160` | Hard cap on simultaneously running effects. When exceeded, the oldest effect is stopped to keep frame times predictable during bursts. |
| `container_node_name` | `String` | `"Sparkform_Layer"` | Name of the node that hosts spawned effects under the current scene. |

<a id="ripple"></a>

Spawns a flattened water/sonar ripple at `at`.

<a id="chain"></a>

Chains a bolt through `from` and every point in `targets`, one hop
per target. Order matters: each hop is revealed after the previous one.

### `blink(from: Vector2, to: Vector2, options: Dictionary = {}) -> BlinkEffect`

<a id="blink"></a>

Teleports visually from `from` to `to`: collapse, streak, burst.

### `frost_burst(at: Vector2, options: Dictionary = {}) -> FrostBurstEffect`

<a id="frost-burst"></a>

Spawns angular ice shards at `at`.

<a id="impact-crack"></a>

Spawns ground-aligned cracks at `at`. Pass `{"surface": Vector2.UP}`

### `shield(target: Node2D, options: Dictionary = {}) -> ShieldBubble`

<a id="shield"></a>

Wraps `target` in a reactive bubble. Call `ShieldBubble.hit` with
an impact point, or `ShieldBubble.stop` to drop it.

### `tether(from: Node2D, to: Node2D, options: Dictionary = {}) -> Tether`

<a id="tether"></a>

Links two nodes with a sagging energy chain.

### `vortex(at: Vector2, options: Dictionary = {}) -> Vortex`

<a id="vortex"></a>

Opens a pull field at `at`: motes spiral in and recycle at the centre.

### `beam(from: Vector2, to: Vector2, options: Dictionary = {}) -> BeamEffect`

<a id="beam"></a>

Creates a persistent beam from `from` to `to`. Keep the returned
node to re-aim it with `BeamEffect.end_at` or end it with
`BeamEffect.stop`.

### `portal(at: Vector2, options: Dictionary = {}) -> PortalEffect`

<a id="portal"></a>

Opens a persistent portal at `at`. Call `PortalEffect.stop` on the
returned node to play the closing animation.

### `rune_circle(target: Node2D, seconds: float = 0.0, options: Dictionary = {}) -> RuneCircle`

<a id="rune-circle"></a>

Adds a cast circle as a child of `target`. `seconds` sets how long
it runs before closing on its own (`0` runs until stopped).

### `trail(target: Node2D, options: Dictionary = {}) -> TrailEffect`

<a id="trail"></a>

Attaches a ribbon trail to `target`. It frees itself when the target
leaves the tree, or earlier with `TrailEffect.stop`.

### `cooldown_ring(target: Node2D, seconds: float = 1.0, options: Dictionary = {}) -> CooldownRing`

<a id="cooldown-ring"></a>

Adds a cooldown ring as a child of `target` and starts it immediately.
Returns the ring so callers can inspect `CooldownRing.progress`,
restart it, or cancel it.

## `VFXEffect`

Extends `Node2D`.

Base class for every one-shot effect in Sparkform.

An effect is a short-lived scene that plays for `duration` seconds and
then emits `finished`. `Sparkform` listens for that signal and
recycles the instance instead of freeing it, so spawning is allocation free
after warm-up.

Subclasses implement the three virtual callbacks below and draw with
`CanvasItem._draw` if they need geometry:

```gdscript
func _on_play() -> void:
    pass                        # configure particles, reset state

func _on_update(progress: float, delta: float) -> void:
    pass                        # progress is 0..1 across the lifetime

func _on_stop() -> void:
    pass                        # tear down / stop emitters
```


### Signals

| Signal | Description |
|---|---|
| `finished` | Emitted exactly once per `play` call, when the effect reaches the end of its lifetime or is stopped early. |

### Properties

**Lifetime**

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | `float` | `0.5` | How long the effect runs, in seconds. |
| `free_on_finish` | `bool` | `true` | Free the node as soon as the effect finishes. Pooled effects spawned through `Sparkform` always set this to `false`. |
| `play_on_ready` | `bool` | `false` | Play the effect as soon as it enters the tree (handy for effects dropped straight into a scene by hand). |


### Methods

#### `play() -> void`

Starts (or restarts) the effect from the beginning.

#### `stop() -> void`

Stops the effect early and emits `finished`. Safe to call when the
effect is already stopped.

#### `is_playing() -> bool`

Returns `true` while the effect is running.

#### `configure(options: Dictionary) -> void`

Applies a dictionary of exported properties by name. Unknown keys log a
warning instead of failing, which keeps the `Sparkform` convenience
methods forgiving.

## `VFXStreaks`

Extends `RefCounted`.

Bridge to the optional C++ streak field (GDExtension).

The extension is a separate, optional build: `tools/build_extension.sh`
compiles `cpp/` against godot-cpp and drops the library into
`addons/sparkform/bin/`. When it is present this class instantiates
`VFXStreakField2D`; when it is not, every method here degrades to a
no-op so the pure-GDScript effects keep working unchanged.


```gdscript
if VFXStreaks.is_available():
    var field := VFXStreaks.create(self, {"head_color": Color.ORANGE})
    VFXStreaks.burst(field, {"count": 500, "spread": TAU})
```


### Methods

#### `is_available() -> bool`

Returns `true` when the compiled extension is loaded.

#### `create(parent: Node, properties: Dictionary = {}) -> Node2D`

Creates a streak field under `parent` and applies `properties`
(any exported property of the C++ node). Returns `null` when the
extension is not available.

#### `burst(field: Node2D, config: Dictionary) -> void`

Emits a burst on `field`. See the C++ class for the accepted keys:
origin, count, direction, spread (radians), speed_min, speed_max,
lifetime_min, lifetime_max.

#### `clear(field: Node2D) -> void`

Removes every live particle.

#### `alive_count(field: Node2D) -> int`

Live particle count, or `0` when unavailable.

## `vfx_shapes`

Extends `RefCounted`.

Procedural outline helpers shared by the effects.

Every effect draws its own geometry, and the "chaos" knob is what makes that
geometry irregular: rings that wobble, cones with torn edges, stars with
uneven spikes. This file holds the maths so each effect does not repeat it.

Effects load it with a relative `preload` rather than a global
class name, so they keep parsing even when the editor's class cache has not
been generated yet.

### Methods

#### `irregular_ring(radius: float, wobble: float, points: int, phase: float, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> PackedVector2Array`

Closed, wobbling ring of `points` vertices. `wobble` is the
fraction of `radius` the outline may stray by.

#### `jagged_cone(direction: Vector2, length: float, half_angle: float, teeth: int, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> PackedVector2Array`

Torn cone for muzzle flashes: apex at the origin, jagged edge facing
`direction`. `teeth` alternates long and short tips.

#### `star_burst(inner: float, outer: float, spikes: int, rotation: float, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> PackedVector2Array`

Uneven star burst, used for flashes and sparkles.

#### `scattered_directions(count: int, direction: Vector2, bias: float, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> Array[Vector2]`

Scatters `count` unit vectors, biased towards `direction` by
`bias` (0 = fully random ring, 1 = straight ahead).
